title: Quick JSON CLI
summary: A small command-line wrapper that pretty-prints JSON.

design_decisions.problem_or_constraint: Raw JSON is hard to read.
design_decisions.alternatives_considered: Existing jq and language-native tools were not compared.
design_decisions.accepted_trade_off: The program loads the entire input into memory and reports raw parser errors.
design_decisions.validation_approach: The author manually piped one object through the command.

testing_strategy: No automated tests or fixtures exist.
security_threat: Very large input can exhaust memory and terminal control characters can be printed. No mitigation is implemented. Residual risk: Input size, terminal escaping, dependency policy, and error disclosure are unaddressed.
production_limitation: No streaming, Windows verification, reusable API, packaging instructions, or extension points.
technical_debt: Choose a license, add tests, document installation and contribution, bound input, and explain why this should exist instead of mature tools.
track_alignment_explanation: It is technically a developer tool, but the public repository lacks a license, installation path, contribution guidance, testing evidence, and credible reusable surface.

ai_disclosure.purposes: Codex was used to author this deliberately synthetic calibration fixture and its structured submission answers.
ai_disclosure.substantially_generated_areas: All fixture source, documentation, tests, and submission narratives are synthetic and AI-assisted.
ai_disclosure.review_validation: The calibration operator reviews files for intended evidence strength, consistency, and absence of real secrets before pinning the commit.
ai_disclosure.rejected_or_changed_suggestion: Generic claims of runtime correctness were rejected because Finch performs static evidence review only.

ai_disclosure_narrative: This entire project is synthetic AI-assisted test data. It represents no participant, deployed product, or real credential.
